long_description:
Overview
Beehive to Business with Rt Hon Winston Peters
We’re privileged to welcome our sixth speaker in our Business to Beehive Leaders Series: Rt Hon Winston Peters, Leader of the New Zealand First Party.
This series brings party leaders to our members for open conversations about their priorities, perspectives, and policy direction.
Join us on Tuesday, 25 August, where the Rt Hon Winston Peters will share his views on the forces shaping New Zealand’s future, and the role business can play within a changing economic, environmental, and social landscape. Mr Peters brings an unparalleled background in New Zealand politics, foreign affairs, and legal practice to the role. His career spans decades of service as a Member of Parliament, Deputy Prime Minister, and Minister of Foreign Affairs, providing deep insight into both domestic governance and international trade.
This is the sixth in our series of high-value discussions designed to give our members direct access to political leaders and a broader understanding of the landscape ahead.
Join us for a thoughtful and engaging discussion as you navigate the lead-up to election day.
Agenda:
7:15 am – Standing breakfast and networking
7:45 am – Address by Rt Hon Winston Peters
8:10 am – Q&A session
8:30 am – Event concludes
Can't make it? Click here to register for the free livestream. Sign up and watch at a time convenient to you.
Part of the ongoing Beehive to Business series, this event is proudly made possible through our partnership with Wellington-based consulting firm Allen + Clarke.

venue: Venue To be Confirmed | Wellington CBDWellington, Wellington Region
long_description:
Overview





Learn the skills, approaches and techniques needed to effectively plan and successfully facilitate a workshop.
Description
The purpose of this course is to provide participants with the skills needed to successfully facilitate a workshop. This course provides an approach and techniques for the effective planning and running of workshops.
Greater emphasis is being placed on skilled business and digital professionals who have the ability to communicate strongly, engage with stakeholders, and elicit a clear result from your team. Workshop facilitation skills, and increasingly online facilitation skills, have never been more important.

The skills and techniques taught on this course will be applicable to all types of workshops. Course participants undertake a realistic workshop facilitation exercise, to reinforce the principles and techniques learnt during the course.

The ‘Workshop Facilitation’ course is delivered by seasoned Equinox consultant practitioners who apply the techniques and practices presented in this course on a daily basis.

Outline
Introduction
Working agreement
Keys to success
Preparation
Workshop facilitation exercise
During the workshop
Risks and mitigations
Follow up
Online facilitation
Retrospective

Learning outcomes
Following the completion of this course, students will be able to:
Have greater awareness of themselves as a workshop facilitator
Understand a process for preparing and running a workshop
Understand the rationale, justification, and roles for workshops
Learn the intricacies of workshop planning
Have applied the techniques for effectively running a workshop

Audience
The audience for this course is business and digital professionals who get involved in producing results through facilitation.

Prerequisites
There are no prerequisites for this course.

id: The Clothes Swap - Wellington CBD-Thistle Hall - UpstairsTe Aro, Wellington-Event Brite
name: The Clothes Swap - Wellington CBD
venue: Thistle Hall - UpstairsTe Aro, Wellington
long_description:
Overview







Fashion waste is one of the Earth's biggest polluters. Let's come together and reduce waste by swapping clothes.
Attend The Clothes Swap and swap up to 10 items that you don't reach for anymore.
How it works:
- Buy a ticket through EventBrite
2 for 1 - $15 (until sold out)
Early bird - $15 (until 30th June or sold out)
General Admission - $20 (1st July until 29th August)
- Bring up to 10 items of clothing that are in good condition - clothing guideline/what to bring below
- Check in your items in 1 hour before the event starts and receive your tokens to swap with. 1 item = 1 token.
- Check in starts at 10am - 11am. The Swap starts at 11:15am - 12:15pm.
- Browse the clothes at the swap event and choose your fabulous new pieces.
- Check out with your tokens and enjoy your new clothes!
- Leftover clothes will be donated
The Clothes Swap Clothing Guidelines
What to bring?
We all want to find good quality clothes to love so we all need to bring good quality clothes to swap.
Please bring garments that are in good condition, not too worn or pilled and with no stains or damage.
Please read our Brand Guidelines via the link below:
https://theclothesswap.mailchimpsites.com/brand-guidelines
Please read our Quality Guidelines via the link below:
https://theclothesswap.mailchimpsites.com/quality-guidelines

When you check in your clothes we’ll have a quick look just to ensure the garments that are coming in are of good quality and are an accepted brand.

Please note: if an item of clothing is an accepted brand but in poor quality, it will not be accepted.
Clothing with no brand labels will also not be accepted.
How to get to Thistle Hall - Upstairs Hall:
The entry to the upstairs hall is around the corner from the entry to the gallery - there'll be a sign. There are stairs inside the door that go up to the upstairs hall which is where the Swap will be or a lift if you need it.

id: BIMinNZ Wellington: Exploring the Future of Digital Delivery-Wellington Faculty of Architecture and Design Innovation / Te Wāhanga Waihanga-HoahoaWellington, Wellington Region-Event Brite

venue: Wellington Faculty of Architecture and Design Innovation / Te Wāhanga Waihanga-HoahoaWellington, Wellington Region
long_description:
Overview




Join us in Poneke for our first ever entirely lady led BIMinNZ!
Join us on 11 August at the Victoria University of Wellington School of Architecture for the first-ever lady-led BIMinNZ. This special evening brings together three outstanding speakers from across New Zealand's built environment to explore the future of digital delivery through the lenses of digital twins, reality capture, and innovation on complex infrastructure projects. From strategic asset management to cutting-edge reality capture technologies and the delivery of Scott Base in Antarctica, this event will showcase how digital thinking is transforming the way we design, construct, and operate our built environment.

This event will take place within the ground floor atrium space of Te Herenga Waka - Victoria University of NZ Te Aro Campus

Anna Whitmore - Allora
Anna Whitmore will present on how applying systems thinking to capital delivery can improve project outcomes by designing digital twins alongside physical assets from the outset. She will explore the importance of establishing a clear vision to align stakeholders, secure sponsorship, and support the people and change aspects of digital transformation.

Kirsty Mackie - Global Survey
Kirsty Mackie is a reality capture specialist from Global Survey. She will explore the latest innovations in reality capture technology, specifically focusing on how SLAM technology is transforming the industry. Expect an overview of the technology and its different applications.

Hanna Hawke - LT McGuinness
Hanna Hawke from LT McGuinness will share insights from her recent work on the Scott Base Redevelopment in Antarctica, exploring how reality capture and digital innovation are supporting one of the world's most remote and challenging construction projects.

long_description:
Overview
A first level qualification in Lego Serious Play with its usual twist of change magic added into the learning experience
Lego® Serious Play® is a world recognized hands on technique for facilitating the exploration of challenges, using unique approaches with inclusive groups as they tackle the ups and downs of personal and professional development opportunities.
This workshop will focus on building your skills as a Lego® Serious Play® (LSP1.0) facilitator.
In day 1 you will be introduced to the benefits of the approach and learn the three core elements of LSP: challenge, build and share for individual, group and connected building. We will also explore the needs for clarity of challenge and using LSP to help define that challenge as well as potential for coaching and facilitating others through change.
In day 2 you will learn how to apply the day 1 learning through practical application of the learning as well as define a workshop and practice facilitating an activity individually and with others. Certification will be awarded to attendees who complete the workshop content and successfully deliver a short, facilitated workshop event at the end of Day 2.
All attendees will go away with an information booklet and guide for undertaking LSP themselves and a Lego Exploration pack.
